argument_summary: The supportable certification theory is narrower than rollout-controls-alone. Admissible evidence supports that aggregate launch readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, while deployment monitoring and rollback are relevant mitigations. The same admissible record also shows the clinical-trial intake segment remains below target, remains exposed in the initial cohort, and is not covered by approved risk acceptance. On that record, the defensible packet is certification expressly conditioned on model-card disclosure of the material limitation for the exposed use case, with monitoring and rollback treated as secondary mitigations rather than as a substitute for disclosure.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is necessary to resolve the audit issue. The argument rests on narrowing the certification rationale to match the admissible policy record.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy and quoted policy text both point the same way: when the affected use case remains exposed, rollout percentage, rollback, and monitoring do not eliminate disclosure duties. Policy compliance is therefore available only in caveated form on this record: certification is supportable if framed as requiring disclosure of the clinical-trial intake limitation, not if framed as cured by rollout controls alone. No admissible evidence supports claiming approved risk acceptance or exclusion of the exposed use case.
concessions: The current record does not contain the actual launch model-card or disclosure text.
The current record does not show approved risk acceptance specific to the exposed clinical-trial intake segment.
The current record does not support any claim that rollout controls alone satisfy the policy requirement.
